Hi team / Alice —

Attached is the single-page topology (redwood_seg_assurance_topology_v2.pdf) and the narrative below — drafted to be copy/paste-ready for your SOC 2 artifact bundle.

Narrative (draft):
Redwood’s Dedicated and Private deployment models enforce tenant segregation through a layered approach: 1) tenancy isolation at the orchestration layer (dedicated GPU pools or customer VPCs), 2) network microsegmentation via per-tenant VLANs and ACLs at the edge, and 3) control-plane partitioning with scoped management endpoints and RBAC-bound keys. Egress and inter-tenant flows are strictly whitelisted; preflight policy gates and automated egress proxies inspect outbound requests. During failover events we retain tenant-affine routing: running replica instances in an isolated tenant slice with least-privilege access to shared services; automatic model-variant fallback preserves availability while degrading to lower-cost runtime variants. These controls collectively minimize cross-tenant data exposure and provide a clear audit trail for SOC 2 control objectives.

Action requested: Alice, can you confirm if the narrative tone is sufficient for Veridian's control owner, or if we should expand the failover section with operational playbook excerpts?

Attachments included: redwood_seg_assurance_topology_v2.pdf

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Platform Security

I've uploaded the segregation matrix draft (segregation_matrix_2026-12-04.xlsx). Key highlights in the sheet: 

- Column A: service name (ingress-proxy, inference-runtime, cache, metrics, control-plane-api)
- Column B: tenancy scope (per-tenant, shared-readonly, control-plane-only)
- Column C: VLAN/NSP tag (e.g., tenant-<id>-vlan), ingress ACLs, egress proxy rules
- Column D: evidence pointer (config blob path / playbook id)

A couple of notes: shared services (metrics, artifact-store) are read-only for tenants and served through a read-proxy that strips sensitive request headers; those proxies live in a separate monitored VLAN with strict egress.

I'll add the config references after a brief cleanup pass. Also attaching the SIG_response_draft_mar-2027.docx with the questions we've answered so far.
